section_summary: This section covers State Department memoranda, correspondence, and reports from early 1948 concerning United States occupation policy and economic reform in Japan, focusing on the deconcentration of excessive economic power and policy paper FEC 230. Major items include internal departmental reviews and an official reply to Senator H. Alexander Smith regarding James Lee Kauffman's report attacking SCAP's economic and labor programs, accompanied by Kauffman's complete 31-page report. The documents also address Chinese press reactions in Shanghai criticizing American economic reconstruction of Japan, discussions with the British Embassy on sterling area trade, and State Department tactics to delay FEC consideration of FEC 230 pending George F. Kennan's return from Japan.

subfiles.summary: Whitman reports Butterworth's objections to providing material to House committee staff director Elliott without prior clearance from FE.
subfiles.title: Material Left with Mr. Elliott, Staff Director, House Foreign Affairs Committee

subfiles.about: Cover memorandum forwarding Whitman's memo to Bohlen regarding procedures for working with Congressional committee staffs.
subfiles.summary: Kirlin forwards Whitman's memo to Bohlen, suggesting a discussion on how best to work with Congressional committee staffs.
subfiles.title: Working with Congressional Committee Staffs

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation with William Yandell Elliott discussing proposed revisions to the House committee staff report on aid to Japan.
subfiles.summary: State Department representatives discuss House staff report additions with Elliott, addressing deconcentration, Japanese security forces, and aid to China.
subfiles.title: Proposed House Foreign Affairs Staff Report "Problems of Interim Aid to Japan"

subfiles.about: Memorandum transmitting the Kauffman report and OE's analysis to George F. Kennan along with Kauffman's biographical background.
subfiles.summary: Claxton transmits the Kauffman report and OE's analysis to Kennan, providing biographical details on Kauffman's legal background in Japan.
subfiles.title: Kauffman Report

subfiles.about: Comprehensive State Department analysis refuting James Lee Kauffman's criticisms of SCAP's economic reform and deconcentration programs in Japan.
subfiles.from: Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: This memorandum provides a comprehensive critique of James Lee Kauffman's report on economic conditions in Japan. It defends SCAP's programs for zaibatsu deconcentration, land reform, labor union development, and progressive taxation as essential measures to build a democratic society immune to extremism. The analysis argues that Japanese economic stagnation stems from wartime destruction and raw material shortages rather than occupation policies, and rejects Kauffman's assertion that reforms foster socialism.
subfiles.title: Analysis of the Kauffman Report

subfiles.about: Draft pages of a State Department reply to Senator H. Alexander Smith defending occupation labor, purge, and deconcentration policies.
subfiles.summary: Draft pages explaining SCAP's implementation of the economic purge, Far Eastern Commission labor directives, and the origins of deconcentration under FEC 230.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to Senator H. Alexander Smith on the Kauffman Report and FEC 230

subfiles.about: Letter answering Senator Smith's inquiry regarding Newsweek's article on the Kauffman report and clarifying U.S. policy on FEC 230 and deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary Lovett responds to Senator Smith regarding a Newsweek article quoting James Lee Kauffman's report and discussing policy paper FEC 230. He delineates State Department policy formulation from Army execution and defends SCAP's labor, agrarian, and anti-monopoly reforms as vital for fostering democratic capitalism. Lovett recounts the origins of FEC 230 from the 1946 deconcentration mission through SWNCC 302, noting the document is currently under re-examination and refuting allegations of improper secrecy.
subfiles.title: Letter to Senator H. Alexander Smith on the Kauffman Report and FEC 230

subfiles.about: Central files record sheet directing the return of file 894.50/2-2048 to the Department of State Central Files.
subfiles.summary: Document file sheet directing return of file 894.50/2-2048 to the Department of State Central Files.
subfiles.title: Central Files Sheet for File 894.50/2-2048

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report criticizing SCAP's economic experimentation, labor laws, deconcentration program, and purge as destructive to Japanese recovery and American interests.
subfiles.summary: In this 31-page report, attorney James Lee Kauffman vigorously criticizes the Allied occupation's economic administration in Japan, advising against American dollar investment under current conditions. He condemns SCAP's deconcentration program under FEC 230, the Anti-Monopoly Law, the Labor Standards Law, and agrarian land redistribution, describing them as socialist experiments administered by inexperienced bureaucrats and theorists. Kauffman highlights runaway inflation, labor indiscipline, and the crippling impact of the economic purge on experienced business leaders like Count Aisuke Kabayama. He urges the immediate termination of economic experimentation, the removal of radical civilian advisers, and the return of industrial management to seasoned leaders to make Japan self-supporting and a bulwark against Soviet expansion.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan as of September 6, 1947

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting Chinese press hostility toward American economic rehabilitation of Japan and recommending detailed public policy statements.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Cabot analyzes hostile reactions in the Shanghai press following his Rotary Club address defending American policy in Japan. Major Chinese newspapers, notably Ta Kung Pao, accused the United States of rebuilding Japanese militarist and industrial dominance in violation of the Potsdam and Cairo declarations while neglecting Chinese needs. Cabot attributes this sentiment to Chinese fears of revived Japanese industrial competition and potential aggression. He urges the State Department to release clear, detailed public statements emphasizing Japan's complete demilitarization, the dismantling of war potential, and the prohibitive cost of occupation to American taxpayers.
subfiles.title: Criticism of United States Economic Policy in Japan

subfiles.about: Letter from the British Embassy querying Whitman's definition of the sterling area in an article on Japanese recovery and enclosing a British study.
subfiles.summary: Ford asks Whitman how the sterling area is defined in his article on Japanese recovery and encloses a confidential British study.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Sterling Area Trade with Japan

subfiles.about: Letter returning the confidential British study and explaining the statistical and geographic definitions of the sterling area used in Whitman's article.
subfiles.summary: Whitman returns the British trade study, clarifying his definitions and data years regarding sterling area trade with Japan.
subfiles.title: Clarification on Sterling Area Trade with Japan

subfiles.about: Briefing memorandum outlining talking points for Under Secretary Lovett's conversation with Under Secretary of the Army Draper concerning strategy for withdrawing support from FEC 230.
subfiles.summary: Wisner outlines the State Department's strategy to withdraw support from FEC 230 without physically pulling the paper from the FEC, stalling discussion until Kennan returns.
subfiles.title: Material for Telephone Conversation with Mr. Draper on Withdrawal of FEC 230
